thin.what is missing: british-raj/ledger/19 and kashmir-and-jammu/ledger/9 record vassal_start 1891 (ending 1947) with hunza-and-nagar as counterpart; this ledger has no mirror. The author reads the schema as putting vassalage only in the suzerain's ledger. Gilgit-Baltistan page: 'in 1891 the states of Hunza and Nagar were formally brought under British suzerainty'; Nagar page: 'Between 1891 and 1947, it maintained a subsidiary alliance with British India'. Add the reciprocal pair if the orchestrator's convention wants mirrors.

The Hunza page: 'recognizing Qing Qianlong Emperor as their suzerain from around 1760', 'From 1847, the Mir of Hunza gave nominal allegiance to China', last tribute 1938; and 'In 1860, the Mir paid tribute to the Dogras'. qing-dynasty and kashmir-and-jammu carry none of this, so Hunza shows as fully independent 1760-1891.

The states lasted inside Pakistan until 1972 (Nagar) and 24 September 1974 (Hunza). The dossier ends them at accession in November 1947, consistent with the neighbours. The orchestrator should decide whether 1947-1974 should be a Pakistani vassalage instead.
